discovery: Theoretical prediction and experimental discovery of topological insulators and the quantum spin Hall effect
motivation: Kane and Mele showed in 2005 that spin-orbit coupling can produce a time-reversal-invariant topological phase, the quantum spin Hall insulator, classified by a Z2 invariant. This established that ordinary band insulators divide into topologically distinct classes. Their work, extended to three dimensions, created the field of topological insulators. In 2007 Molenkamp's group gave the decisive experimental proof. Using exquisitely controlled HgTe/CdTe quantum wells, they observed quantized edge conductance that appeared only above a critical well thickness, as theory predicted. This discovery launched a worldwide effort in topological materials. It directly enabled the quantum anomalous Hall effect, Majorana platforms and topological superconductivity, and it opened routes to dissipationless electronics and fault-tolerant quantum information. Theory predicted a new state of matter and painstaking materials growth realised it, a model of how physics advances. Topology is now a central organising principle of condensed matter physics.
